caption:
Buffer measures carousels at 6.90% and Reels at 3.31%. Socialinsider measures carousels at 0.50% and Reels at 0.48%. Both are correct.

Buffer divides by reach. Socialinsider divides by followers. Same platform, same formats, numbers an order of magnitude apart — because nobody said out loud what they were dividing by.

This is the real reason your reporting feels untrustworthy, and why every "benchmark" article you read contradicts the last one. It usually isn't bad data. It's an unlabelled denominator.

It also explains something more uncomfortable: it's very easy to pick whichever denominator makes the month look good, and most people doing it aren't even being dishonest — they just grabbed the number the tool showed them.

Fix it once. Decide what you divide by, write it on every chart, and keep it the same forever. Your month-over-month comparisons become real, and the monthly argument about whether the numbers are good disappears.

If your agency can't tell you their denominator, that's the whole audit.
